solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Remove cream, curdled

parts.note: the pick of the bunch is its cream, the very best
milk that has curdled has gone off

explanation.surface: A dairy instruction: skim off the cream because the milk has turned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remove' and 'cream' look like one kitchen instruction, but 'Remove' is the definition and 'cream' a noun meaning the best.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick off is to take things away one at a time, or to shoot targets singly, so it means remove.

clue.text: Spot member occupying mansion

indicators.note: the member lives inside the big house

parts.note: a pile is a large, grand house
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A spotted politician has moved into a grand house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spot' looks like a verb but is a blemish.
explanation.definitionFit: A pimple is a small raised blemish on the skin, a spot.

clue.text: Racket in decent condition put away

parts.note: a con is a swindle, a racket
fine means in good health or state

explanation.surface: A tennis racket in good shape has been stored.
explanation.definitionFit: To confine someone is to shut them up or lock them away, which is to put them away.

clue.text: Giant bullied Hearts players

parts.note: an orc is a monster or ogre of folklore

indicators.note: the word hearts is pushed around into a new order

explanation.surface: A giant pushed around the Hearts football team.
explanation.walkthrough: Hearts is the Edinburgh football club Heart of Midlothian, so 'players' looks like its team; it means musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestra is a large group of instrumental musicians, the players.

clue.text: Creative works penned by English novelist succeeded, initially

indicators.note: the works are enclosed inside the writer's name

parts.note: E. M. Forster wrote A Passage to India
art means creative works collectively

explanation.surface: An English novelist's creative works are described as successful at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penned' looks like writing with a pen, but here it means enclosed, as in a sheep pen; 'initially' looks like a first-letter signal but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: For starters is an idiom meaning to begin with, so first of all.

clue.text: Lover, on leaving a country in fact, missing every second

indicators.note: the remaining pieces are placed in the kept letters of fact
dropping every second letter of the word fact keeps only its odd letters
the word on departs from the country, so those letters are deleted

parts.note: a nation is a country
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lover leaves a country and finds, in fact, that something is missing every other time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on leaving' leaves NATI; 'missing every second' keeps F and C, and 'in' puts ANATI between them. 'Lover' means an enthusiast, not a romantic partner.
explanation.definitionFit: A lover in the sense of a devotee or enthusiast is a fan, and a fanatic is an extreme one.

clue.text: Rage following another defeat, all kicking off

indicators.note: each word starts, or kicks off, with the letter taken

explanation.surface: A football fan is furious after another loss, with the whole crowd kicking off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kicking off' is British slang for starting a fight, but here it picks the first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A rage is a craze or passing fashion, as in all the rage, so a fad.

clue.text: Arctic fleet?

definitions.meaning: bitingly cold, as the Arctic is
... also means quick, nimble, so fleet of foot

explanation.surface: A question about a fleet of ships sailing polar seas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fleet' suggests ships, but here it is an adjective meaning swift.
explanation.definitionFit: Nippy means both cold and quick.

clue.text: Spar, a post most hollow at sea

indicators.note: confused, all at sea, so the letters are rearranged
a hollow word has its insides taken out, keeping only the outer letters

explanation.surface: A spar or post on a ship at sea, mostly hollow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hollow' keeps M and T of MOST; 'at sea' rearranges them with A POST.
explanation.definitionFit: A topmast is a ship's mast above the lower mast, a spar.

clue.text: Mafia boss, one in time for martial art

parts.note: a capo is a head of a Mafia family

indicators.note: the numeral sits inside the period of time

parts.note: an era is a span of time
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A Mafia boss arrives just in time for some martial arts.
explanation.definitionFit: Capoeira is a Brazilian martial art that blends fighting with dance and music.

clue.text: My better worker filed beautifully?

parts.note: a man is a worker, as in management and men
read as the speaker's own, the one I
a patient who is better has been cured

explanation.surface: Someone praising their best employee, who apparently filed something very neatly.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'My better worker' as 'the worker I made better': MAN I CURED. 'filed' is about fingernails, not paperwork, and the question mark flags the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Manicured nails have been trimmed and shaped with a file, so they are filed beautifully.

clue.text: Father out of bed, as device making breakfast?

parts.note: pop is an informal word for father
someone out of bed is up

explanation.surface: Dad has got up early as a gadget that cooks breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a pop-up toaster, so the question mark marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A pop-up toaster ejects the toast when done, a breakfast appliance known by that feature.

clue.text: Nothing in old money for European runner

indicators.note: the zero is set inside the currency

parts.note: lire were the money of Italy before the euro
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone has nothing left in their old currency, perhaps a European athlete fallen on hard times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runner' is a crossword term for a river, not an athlete.
explanation.definitionFit: The Loire is France's longest river, and rivers run, so it is a European runner.

clue.text: Something sweet I pulled out of a sticky pie before cooking

indicators.note: food being cooked is changed, so the remaining letters are rearranged
the letter I is taken out of the following words

explanation.surface: A baker removes something from a sticky pie before baking it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pulled out of' removes one I from A STICKY PIE, and 'cooking' rearranges the remaining eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipsy cake is a sponge pudding soaked in wine or sherry, so it is a dessert.

clue.text: Answer more questions around start of interrogation, showing no emotion

indicators.note: the quiz phrase wraps around the letter taken

parts.note: a contestant who answers more questions passes on fewer, so pass on less

indicators.note: only the opening letter of interrogation is taken

explanation.surface: A quiz contestant answers more under interrogation, staying cool and unemotional.
explanation.walkthrough: In a quiz you can say pass instead of answering, so answering more means you PASS ON LESS; 'around' puts I in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Passionless means lacking strong feeling, so showing no emotion.

clue.text: Worker on organ, cosmetic surgeon?

definitions.meaning: an organ is a newspaper or magazine
jokingly, a plastic surgeon edits a person's facial features

explanation.surface: A worker on some body part is described as a cosmetic surgeon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' looks medical, which the surgeon reinforces, but here it means a publication.
explanation.definitionFit: On a newspaper, a features editor commissions longer articles; a surgeon reshaping a face would be editing features.

clue.text: Ignoring leader in reshuffle, shift around each Tory minister

indicators.note: the reduced garment goes around the other pieces
the leader is left out of the garment

parts.note: a shift is a simple straight dress

indicators.note: the leader of reshuffle is its first letter

parts.note: con is short for Conservative, a Tory

explanation.surface: A cabinet reshuffle in which a Tory minister is shifted around, but without the party leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reshuffle' and 'shift' look like anagram signals; neither is. 'Ignoring' leaves DESS, which goes 'around' the rest. The minister is a church one, not a government one.
explanation.definitionFit: A deaconess is a woman deacon in some churches, a minister of religion.

clue.text: Baseball player put champions in first place

parts.note: to champion a cause is to back it, so champions means backs
the top is first place in a ranking

explanation.surface: A baseball player puts winning champions in the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'champions' is a verb, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A backstop is the catcher in baseball, who stops balls from behind the batter.

clue.text: As characters here (initials), positioned thus?

parts.note: the first letters of As, characters and here are A, C and H, which run in the order of the letters A to Z

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark about how some letters on the page have been laid out.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the opening letters of As, characters, here run in A-to-Z order, so they are arranged that way.

clue.text: Item originally found in plain case

indicators.note: the letter is set inside the synonym for plain

parts.note: patent means obvious or plain

indicators.note: taken at its origin, so just its first letter

explanation.surface: An item was first discovered in a plain box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' looks like a container but means a medical case.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor's case is a person under treatment, a patient.

clue.text: Wayward lassie ultimately into drink?

indicators.note: the letters go into the drink

parts.note: a latte is a milky coffee

indicators.note: only the final letter of each word is taken

explanation.surface: A wild young woman who has, in the end, taken to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' takes the last letters D and E of 'Wayward lassie'; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladette is a young woman who behaves boisterously, notably with heavy drinking, like the lads.

clue.text: Writer of nonsense needing books picked up

parts.note: Edward Lear wrote nonsense verse such as The Owl and the Pussy-cat
NT is the New Testament, a collection of books

explanation.surface: A nonsense writer needs to have books collected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' suggests collecting, but means acquired knowledge.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick up a skill is to acquire it, which is to have learnt it.

clue.text: Tackle issue about wagon for frontiersman

indicators.note: the two pieces go around the vehicle, enclosing it

parts.note: kit is equipment, as fishing tackle is
a son is offspring, issue in legal language
a car is a wagon, like a railway car

explanation.surface: Gather the gear and deal with a problem concerning the cart for a pioneer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts KIT and SON either side of CAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Kit Carson was a nineteenth-century American scout and trapper on the Western frontier.

clue.text: Letter a problem, initially dropped?

indicators.note: the first letter of the problem falls away

parts.note: a hitch is a snag or problem

explanation.surface: A letter of complaint about a problem that was dropped at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface also hints that the letter itself is often dropped at the start of words, as in 'appy for 'happy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Aitch is the written name of the letter H.

clue.text: Cambridge crew losing first classic

indicators.note: the crew's name drops its first letter

parts.note: Goldie is the Cambridge reserve crew in the Boat Race

explanation.surface: A Cambridge rowing crew loses its opening Boat Race, a classic contest.
explanation.walkthrough: The Boat Race is the annual Oxford v Cambridge rowing race on the Thames; Goldie is Cambridge's reserve boat. 'losing first' drops its G.
explanation.definitionFit: An oldie is an old song or film still loved, a golden oldie, so a classic.

clue.text: Ignoring every other part, turn exact handle

indicators.note: skipping alternate letters keeps the first, third, fifth and so on of the following words

explanation.surface: Instructions for a lock: skip some parts and turn the handle precisely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'handle' looks like a door handle, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To treat someone or something is to deal with or handle them in a certain way.

clue.text: Host current monarch

parts.note: present means current, existing now
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A host is described as the current monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A presenter fronts a TV or radio show, hosting it.

clue.text: Spot Dickens character

definitions.meaning: a spot on dice or dominoes

explanation.definitionFit: Pip names both a small spot or mark and Dickens's orphan narrator.

clue.text: Appear happy after sales talk

indicators.note: happy is placed after the sales talk

parts.note: a pitch is a salesman's patter
up means cheerful, in good spirits

explanation.surface: Someone looks pleased after hearing a sales pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: To pitch up is informal for to arrive or turn up, so to appear.

clue.text: Unconvincing South American setter drops in

parts.note: US means American

indicators.note: the word in is dropped from the setting agent

parts.note: pectin is what makes jam set
taken as written

explanation.surface: A South American crossword setter pays a visit, but the story sounds fishy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' suggests the compiler or a dog; it is pectin, the jam setter, losing IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A suspect story is doubtful, one you cannot quite believe.
